questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a PERFECTLY COMPETITIVE market?
options: A) Few large firms dominate the market
C) Many small firms sell identical products
questions.correct_answer: C) Many small firms sell identical products
questions.explanation: Perfect competition requires MANY small firms selling IDENTICAL (homogeneous) products. No single firm can affect the market price — they are PRICE TAKERS. Few dominant firms = oligopoly. Differentiated products = monopolistic competition. High barriers = monopoly.

questions.text: In perfect competition, the demand curve facing an individual firm is:
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='180' viewBox='0 0 350 180'><rect width='350' height='180' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><line x1='40' y1='140' x2='330' y2='140' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='20' x2='40' y2='140' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='70' x2='330' y2='70' stroke='#f43f5e' stroke-width='3'/><text x='140' y='60' fill='#f43f5e' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>D = MR = Price (Horizontal)</text><text x='320' y='155' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>Q</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The individual firm faces a HORIZONTAL demand curve because it is a PRICE TAKER. It can sell ANY quantity at the market price but CANNOT sell above the market price. The demand curve is PERFECTLY ELASTIC — consumers will switch to another firm if price rises.

questions.text: A perfectly competitive firm maximizes profit where:
questions.explanation: Profit is maximized where MC = MR. In perfect competition, MR = Price (because the firm is a price taker). Therefore, the profit-maximizing condition is MC = Price. The firm produces where the additional cost of one more unit equals the additional revenue.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of perfect competition?
questions.explanation: Perfect competition assumes HOMOGENEOUS (IDENTICAL) products — NOT differentiated. Product differentiation is a feature of MONOPOLISTIC competition. Perfect information, free entry/exit, and many participants ARE assumptions of perfect competition.

questions.text: Examine the diagram. What does the shaded area represent?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='200' viewBox='0 0 350 200'><rect width='350' height='200' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><line x1='40' y1='170' x2='330' y2='170' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='20' x2='40' y2='170' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='70' x2='330' y2='70' stroke='#f43f5e' stroke-width='3'/><path d='M 50 160 Q 140 100 200 40 Q 280 20 320 30' stroke='#facc15' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><path d='M 50 165 Q 150 120 330 60' stroke='#14b8a6' stroke-width='2' fill='none'/><rect x='100' y='70' width='120' height='40' fill='rgba(20, 184, 166, 0.3)' stroke='none'/><text x='160' y='90' text-anchor='middle' fill='#14b8a6' font-size='11' font-weight='bold'>Profit Area</text><text x='320' y='185' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>Q</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The shaded area above ATC and below price represents ECONOMIC PROFIT. When Price > ATC, the firm earns economic profit. The rectangle shows (Price - ATC) × Quantity = Total Economic Profit. In the long run, free entry eliminates this profit.

questions.text: In the LONG RUN, a perfectly competitive firm earns:
options: C) Zero economic profit (normal profit only)
questions.correct_answer: C) Zero economic profit (normal profit only)
questions.explanation: In the LONG RUN, perfectly competitive firms earn ZERO ECONOMIC PROFIT (but still earn NORMAL profit — enough to stay in business). If firms earn profit, new firms enter, increasing supply and lowering price. If firms lose money, firms exit, decreasing supply and raising price. This continues until zero economic profit.

questions.text: If Price < ATC but Price > AVC in the short run, the firm should:
options: B) Continue producing in the short run
questions.correct_answer: B) Continue producing in the short run
questions.explanation: If Price > AVC (but < ATC), the firm covers its variable costs AND contributes toward fixed costs. It's better to continue producing in the short run and lose less than shutting down. If Price < AVC, the firm should SHUT DOWN because it can't even cover variable costs.

questions.text: The INDUSTRY demand curve in perfect competition is:
questions.explanation: While the individual FIRM faces a HORIZONTAL demand curve, the INDUSTRY faces a normal DOWNWARD-SLOPING demand curve. This is because at the industry level, lower prices attract more total buyers. The industry price is determined by intersection of industry supply and demand.

questions.text: Which real-world market is CLOSEST to perfect competition?
questions.explanation: Agricultural markets approximate perfect competition: MANY small farmers produce IDENTICAL products (all wheat is basically the same), no single farmer affects the world price, and new farmers can enter freely. Soft drinks and smartphones are oligopolies/ differentiated products.

questions.text: A firm's shutdown point occurs when:
questions.explanation: The SHUTDOWN POINT occurs when Price falls below AVC. At this point, the firm can't even cover its variable costs (labor, raw materials), so it should SHUT DOWN and only pay fixed costs. The firm loses LESS by shutting down than by continuing production.
